haiku-low.q1: Before ready. The HTTP server listens first, then the gate loads all three secrets. /healthz returns 503 until they load, then 200.
haiku-low.q2: It retries 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero. The pod crash-loops and the rollout halts. Old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected.
haiku-low.q3: Every 5 minutes plus up to 30 seconds jitter, it fetches the latest version and swaps if changed. On failure it keeps the last good value, logs a warning and increments a failure metric.
haiku-low.q4: Held in memory only, in SecretCache snapshots. Never in logs, output, exception messages, disk or environment variables. Only version ids are logged.
haiku-low.q5: Prod pod identity orders-api-prod reads prod secrets. The Security on-call role writes them. Engineers can read dev only and cannot read prod values.
haiku-low.q6: The keys stay in git history and old registry images, so they remain exposed. Disabling at providers removes their function, and deletion after the soak period finishes it.
haiku-low.q7: Each provider call reads the current snapshot when made and puts that key in the Authorization Bearer header. Clients no longer copy the key at construction time.
haiku-low.q8: Each of the 4 pods must report the latest version id via the secret_version metric or version-change logs, after one refresh cycle plus margin. Old keys must show zero provider use for about 30 minutes.
haiku-low.q9: Store access (Step 1), then new keys issued and loaded into store (Step 2), then app switched to store and config keys removed (Steps 3-4), then old keys disabled (Step 6).
haiku-low.q10: make run sets APP_ENV=dev and reads orders-api/dev/* using the developer role, which can read dev only. Those values are sandbox keys, not live keys.
haiku-low.q11: The attempt fails, because one attempt needs all three secrets and a failed attempt keeps nothing. It retries up to 3 times, 2 seconds apart, then exits non-zero.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED. The plan does not set a rotation cadence; Security has not decided whether or how often keys rotate.

sonnet.q1: The HTTP server starts listening first, then the startup gate loads all three secrets. The app marks itself ready (/healthz 200) only after a full successful load; before that /healthz returns 503.
sonnet.q2: The gate retries (3 retries, 4 attempts, 2 s apart), then exits non-zero. Kubernetes restarts it, so the pod crash-loops with backoff. The rolling deploy (maxUnavailable 0) halts and the old pods keep serving, so live traffic is unaffected (a stalled deploy, not an outage).
sonnet.q3: A timer every 5 minutes (plus up to 30 s jitter per pod) fetches the latest version of each secret; if the version id changed, a new snapshot is swapped in. If a read fails, the last good snapshot is kept indefinitely (no max age), a warning is logged, secret_refresh_failures_total is incremented, and an alert on staleness (threshold/recipient not decided) is meant to catch it.
sonnet.q4: Held only in process memory, in the SecretCache as immutable snapshots {value, version_id, fetched_at}. Never logged, printed, put in exception messages, written to disk, or put in environment variables (only version ids are logged). Also no mounted secret files or Kubernetes Secret objects; core dumps turned off or not collected.
sonnet.q5: Read prod: the orders-api-prod service identity (orders-api/prod/* only). Write prod: only the Security on-call role. Engineers can read dev only and cannot read prod values.
sonnet.q6: The keys stay in git history (and old images in the registry), and the plan does not rewrite history, so they remain exposed and are treated as leaked. They are made harmless by rotating: new keys are issued, old keys are disabled (Step 6) and then deleted after a soak (Step 7), so they are inert.
sonnet.q7: Clients no longer copy the key in __init__. On each HTTP call to a provider the client reads the current snapshot from the cache (e.g. secrets.get('payments_api_key')) and puts it in the Authorization: Bearer header. A retried call re-reads the snapshot; one request uses one snapshot.
sonnet.q8: Step 5: each of the 4 prod pods must report the store's latest version id for all three secrets (secret_version metric or version-change log lines), waiting at least one 5-minute refresh cycle plus margin. Also each old key must show zero use at its provider (last-used time) for a Security-set window (suggested 30 min) after the last old pod stops, and every other workload using the keys must be inventoried and migrated.
sonnet.q9: Step 0 confirm provider capabilities; 1 create store namespaces, KMS keys and access policy; 2 issue new provider keys and load them into the store (v1) with old keys still active; 3 build/verify the new code in dev (merge PR that switches app to the store, cleans config/app.yaml, adds CI guard and marker); 4 rolling prod deploy; 5 confirm; 6 disable old keys at providers; 7 soak then delete old keys; 8 marker/rollback lockout (before Step 6); 9 CI guard/runbook. Removing keys from the committed file happens in the Step 3 PR merge (after keys are in the store, before prod promotion); key rotation at providers happens in Step 2 (new keys) and Steps 6-7 (old keys disabled/deleted).
sonnet.q10: From the store at orders-api/dev/*, via make run (APP_ENV=dev), using the developer's dev identity/role, which can read dev only. The values are sandbox keys, not live keys. No fallback to a file or to prod; the prod identity is refused.
sonnet.q11: The attempt fails (any one failing or missing fails the whole attempt, and nothing is kept). It retries all three up to 3 more times, 2 s apart; if still failing, it logs secret names and error classes and exits non-zero, never becoming ready.
sonnet.q12: NOT STATED. Scheduled rotation cadence is undecided (open question); Security has not decided whether or how often keys rotate.
